verified_against: Amazon Seller Central product image requirements
_note: Thresholds live here, not in code, so the number the UI shows and the number the eval measures cannot drift. A threshold change is a dated, reviewable diff. `tier` drives how the UI renders a check: rule_exact = arithmetic on metadata and cannot be wrong; measured = pixel statistics with published precision/recall; advisory = a signal, explicitly not a verdict.

aspect_ratio._why_advisory: Amazon has no hard main-image aspect-ratio requirement for most categories; square is a recommendation. Emitting pass/fail here would be a fabricated verdict with arithmetic behind it.

image_count._why_phrasing_matters: This check sees only the images handed to it, so it reports n_images_supplied and says 'you supplied N', never 'your listing has N'. The cap is category-dependent, which is what the old hardcoded 'Image count (only 3, need 7+)' stub got wrong.

white_background._why_two_statistics: exact_white_frac is the rule (pure white). near_white_frac with a neutrality term (max-min channel spread) catches a faint cream or blue-grey cast that a luminance-only test passes. Reporting the modal RGB lets the user see '(248,248,248), not (255,255,255)' instead of just a failure.
white_background._why_min_channel_is_240: Not 250. At 250 an off-white 248 background reads as FOREGROUND, which both makes the warn path unreachable and corrupts the product mask. 240 is the standard band and still rejects a 230 grey.
white_background._why_max_band_product_frac: Caps the product-exclusion. Excluding border pixels that belong to a component reaching the centre stops a wide compliant product from reading as a dirty background - but with a genuinely grey or coloured background the WHOLE image is one non-white component reaching the centre, so exclusion claims the entire band and leaves nothing to measure. Past this cap the premise no longer holds: a non-white region covering essentially the whole border is far better explained by a non-white background, so the raw band is measured instead and the check can fail as it should.
white_background._why_modal_white_passes: A JPEG-compressed pure-white background has few EXACTLY-255 pixels near product edges because of ringing, so exact_white_frac alone false-warns on a compliant image. If the modal colour is (255,255,255) and essentially every band pixel is near-white, it is a white background with compression noise, and that passes.

frame_occupancy._why_bbox_not_silhouette: Amazon's '85% of the frame' is conventionally the product's bounding box, not its silhouette area. A pair of earbuds fills ~40% of its own bbox, so a silhouette reading fails nearly every compliant listing. bbox_occupancy is the verdict; silhouette_occupancy is reported beside it so a reader can check the interpretation instead of trusting it.

background_artifacts._why_this_replaces_text_detection: The rule is that the background must be pure white, so any connected non-white component on the background that is not the product is a violation regardless of what it is - badge, watermark, border, starburst, prop. The check never has to classify the artifact, which is why its precision is high.

off_product_text._how_it_works: Local ONNX text DETECTION only - no recognition, no VLM, no API. The detector returns boxes; the semantic question ('did the seller overlay this text, or is it printed on the product?') then reduces to GEOMETRY against the background mask this module already computes: centroid in the background mask = overlaid violation; centroid in the product mask = printed on the product and allowed; overlapping the product but extending well past it = banner. So the check that looked like it needed a VLM needs a 62 MB detector plus a rule we already have.
off_product_text._why_not_a_vlm: A hosted VLM would forfeit determinism, which is the whole reason the rest of this module is computed rather than judged. A pinned local ONNX model is deterministic given its input, so the compliance eval stays repeatable, CI-runnable, secret-free and free of a noise floor. It also costs nothing per call and consumes no LLM rate limit.
off_product_text._known_gap: Text overlaid ON TOP of the product region reads as printed-on-product under the geometric rule. Mitigated partially by the banner heuristic. Measure this case separately in the eval rather than claiming it is handled.

image_role._how_it_works: CLIP zero-shot against fixed role prompts. The prompt text embeddings are PRECOMPUTED OFFLINE once and shipped as a small .npy, so the runtime needs only the vision tower - which is already required for near-duplicate detection. Zero additional model at serving time.
image_role._why_this_is_free: Category-level semantics is what CLIP is actually good at, unlike instance identity. And because the prompts are fixed, no text encoder ships.

prohibited_content._honest_limitation: This is the one semantic check a local model does NOT do well. 'Props or accessories not included in the purchase' requires knowing what the purchase includes, and competitor-logo detection needs a logo dataset. Only the two narrow signals above are attemptable via CLIP zero-shot. The full check is NOT claimed - it stays out of scope until there is either labeled data or a measured reason to add a hosted VLM.

_tiers.rule_exact: Arithmetic on image metadata. Cannot be wrong. Drives the headline.
_tiers.measured: A pixel statistic with published precision/recall. Drives the headline.
_tiers.advisory: A signal that is explicitly not a verdict. Never drives the headline.
_tiers.model: A learned-model judgement. Reported and labelled, shipped with its measured agreement against hand labels, and NEVER drives the headline or overrides a computed verdict - the same guard that keeps aspect_ratio from turning a compliant listing red. All model checks run as LOCAL pinned ONNX, so they stay deterministic and the eval stays repeatable; a hosted model would forfeit exactly the property that motivated computing the rest.

_model_runtime_gate.measure_before_enabling: RSS delta of the loaded ONNX sessions inside the service container, against its 512 MB cap. Weights are only part of it - the onnxruntime arena does not reliably return memory to the OS, and the failure signal is a silent exit 137.
_model_runtime_gate.note: No off-the-shelf int8 vision-only export exists in Xenova/clip-vit-base-patch32; quantize_dynamic it here and publish the measured recall delta. Verify the upstream license (openai/clip-vit-base-patch32 is MIT; the Xenova mirror does not declare one).

main_image_only._why: Amazon's pure-white background, 85% frame occupancy, and no-marks-on-the-background requirements apply to the MAIN image only. Secondary images are explicitly permitted lifestyle backgrounds, props, in-use scenes, text and graphics. Applying these three as verdicts to every image in a set would fail a seller's perfectly compliant lifestyle photo against a rule that does not govern it - wrong more often than right on any real listing, which is exactly the failure this module is arranged to prevent.
main_image_only._when_role_is_unknown: Downgraded to advisory, not silently applied and not silently dropped. The measurement is still reported - it is useful - but it is not a claim. The scraped-page path cannot identify which image is the main one, so it always lands here.
